characters.name: In General
characters.description: Adaptational Angst Upgrade: In the films and original sitcom, the Addamses are aCreepy FamilyofPerky Gothswho are unaware of how strange they are compared to the rest of the world, with things like witch-burnings and angry mobs just being another fun part of their lifestyle. Here, they fall under a minority of monster-people historically subjected toFantastic Racism, their ancestor Goody Addams being a prominent figure in a historical genocide. Additionally, they are subject to interpersonal angst that differs from other depictions of the family, as Wednesday has begun to close off from her mother, and Gomez and Morticia are entangled in a murder incident from the past. Adaptational Wimp: Unlike other versions of the Addams Family, theirWednesdaycounterparts are a bit less eccentric and not impervious at all to pain or anything life-threatening.Gomez and Morticia are absolutely terrified of Garrett when he breaks into the school, and Gomez even says that his life flashed before his eyes while attempting to defend himself. Thing and Wednesday herself alsocome very closeto dying at the hands of Season 1's villains. Ascended Extra: All of them have more screentime and more relevance to the plot in season 2 than they had in season 1. Bizarre Taste in Food: Just one of their eccentricities. Gomez and Pugsley eat potpourri like potato chips, and Fester drinks old ketchup. They also enjoy things like cooked roadkill, rats, etc. Character Exaggeration: While Gomez and Morticia havealwaysbeen depicted as aHappily Marriedcoupledeeply and unabashedly in love with each other(it's one of their signature traits), this version dials it up to comical extremes. They can barely gofive minuteswithout making out with each other (even when one of them islocked up in a jail cell), to the point thatWednesday frequently has to tell them to knock it off.

characters.name: Wednesday Addams
characters.description: The eldest daughter of the Addams family and the titular protagonist.

characters.name: Enid Sinclair
characters.description: Wednesday's roommate, who is a werewolf from San Francisco and her polar opposite. Action Girl:Once she finally transforms into a werewolf, she can even take on a Hyde and hold her own for a while. Afraid of Blood: Faints as Wednesday hands her gory pictures. Implied to have fainted for similar reasons before as well. She gets over it by the time of season 2, pranking Wednesday into thinking she's dead by smearing herself with blood and jam, which she then cheerfully eats.Enid:Wednesday, I don't really feel...[faints]Wednesday:[to Thing]Fetch the smelling salts.Again. All-Loving Heroine: She seems genuinely excited about meeting new people. When she first meets Wednesday, she reaches for a hug, only for Wednesday to recoil. Badass Adorable:Enid is perky, sweet and adorable. She also possesses claws sharp enough to tear apart metal, and can easily open locked doors that even no one else can open.In her fullwerewolf form, she's strong enough to overpower the monster...with a dyed pink fluff of hair on her head.

characters.name: Bianca Barclay
characters.description: A siren and the reigning queen bee of Nevermore Academy. Academic Athlete: Is the ace of the fencing team and a brilliant student. The Ace: It's easy to see why she initially forms such a strong rivalry with Wednesday, considering they're both top students, fencing aces, extremely competitive and possess leadership qualities. Alliterative Name: Bianca Barclay. However, it's actually an alias as her mother called her Brandy Jane. Alpha Bitch: Played with. Bianca is the Queen Bee of the school, being a rude, arrogantJerkass. However, later episodes reveal she has insecurities, and loathes the idea of using her powers to control someone's mind, and that she's not really that bad of a person. This makes her more of aLovable Alpha Bitch.

characters.name: Ajax Petropolus
characters.description: A gorgon stoner whom Enid is interested in. Amicable Exes:With Enid by the end of Season 2. After Dort is dealt with, he's ready to move on from their less-than-ideal breakup after accepting that neither of them are at fault for Enid's feelings changing and asks her if she just wants to be friends now, which she happily accepts. Big Damn Heroes:Him calling out Dort's name when he threatens Bianca with her life has him letting go of her just enough for Bianca to escape and Ajax to petrify him. And right on the spot where the chandelier he lights up falls and breaks him to pieces. Informed Flaw: The official character announcement calls him shy and awkward, but he doesn’t come across as such in the show. He actually seems to willingly go against this for Enid.Ajax:Gorgons are taught not to engage. You know, I don’t want to accidentally stone someone. Kindhearted Simpleton: He's slow on the uptake, but a friendly, easygoing guy nevertheless.Eugenejust thinks he's an idiot (but then, he's also jealous).Eugene:That gorgon is a moron!The "simpleton" part is a lot moredownplayedin Season 2, as he picks up thathis relationship with Enid is deteriorating after the new school year starts, and that things are far from fine with Bianca as the issues of Morning Song start to come to light.

characters.name: Xavier Thorpe
characters.description: A popular Nevermore artist, and Wednesday's childhood acquaintance. Art Initiates Life: This is Xavier's personal power. He can conjure up to life anything he draws or paints - but as Wednesday proves, just hitting the resulting product is enough to reduce it to the material it was conjured up from. Berserk Button: Being manipulated. This is the reason he broke up with Bianca, as he couldn't stop believing that she would or had used her Siren abilities on him. When he discovers that Wednesday is lying to him for her investigation of the monster's identity, he also lashes out at her. Betty and Veronica: He is the Veronica to Wednesday's Archie and Tyler's Betty, being the popular guy with theloner artist personato Tyler's safe, open-mindednormie.However, it'sinvertedafter the reveal that Tyler is the Hyde monster. Blessed with Suck: Xavier doesn't necessarily have full control over the drawings he brings to life, likethe drawing of the Hyde thatattacks him.

characters.name: Eugene Ottinger
characters.description: A friendless geek who loves bees. The Beastmaster: He can control bees. Season 2 expands that to other insects. Bee-Bee Gun: As mentioned before, he has the power over bees. Beware the Nice Ones: He's a perfectly friendly and upbeat young man, but has zero problemsiccing thousands of bees upon Thornhill in the finale while calling her abitchfor messing with Nevermore. Big Damn Heroes: Wednesday wouldprobably be good as dead from Laurel's bullet, had he not arrived just in time to summon his bees in throwing Laurel off-balance.

characters.name: Yoko Tanaka
characters.description: A vampire in Enid's social circle. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Disappeared after season one and is not referenced or mentioned by any of the characters. Cool Shades: Due to her eyes being more sensitive to light, she always wears dark glasses during the day, only taking them off at night. Other vampires, including her family, also wear them for similar reasons. Daywalking Vampire: While her eyes are more sensitive to light, causing her to always wear sunglasses during the day, the sun is not harmful to her at all and she can walk around in direct sunlight with everyone else with no issue. Properly Paranoid: She and Divina seem wary of Enid bringing Lucas Walker to the Rave'N.Lucas turns out to have been planning a prank that would crash the Rave'N, and is using Enid to make sure it happens.

characters.name: Josephine Wilks
characters.description: A friend to AgnesDeMillewho helps Wednesday in her investigations. Ascended Fangirl: Like Agnes, Josephine is a big fan of Wednesday. Agnes winds up recruiting her to help Wednesday in some of the early episodes of season 2. Humanshifting: Josephine's outcast ability, which allows her to access the deceased Sheriff Galpin's phone inCall of the Woe.

characters.name: Pugsley Addams
characters.description: Wednesday's younger brother. Adaptational Dye-Job: While Pugsley's a blonde in the original comic strips, this version has black hair, giving him a stronger resemblance to the rest of the family. This is more in line with the previous live action adaptations, which also give him dark hair. Adaptational Intelligence: While he's certainly no genius, Pugsley does come across as considerably less of an idiot than he's usually portrayed as, particularly in Season 2 where he's starting to show signs of maturity. That said, he can still be overly naive and trusting, asSlurp/Isaacdemonstrates. Adaptational Wimp: Most previous versions of Pugsley wouldn't let a bunch of bullies shove him into a locker. It does however allow anEstablishing Character Momentfor Wednesday. Ascended Extra: He's mainly around in Season 1 to show that the rest of the Addams family exists in this universe. He appears much more prominently in Season 2, now that he's a student at Nevermore.

characters.name: Bruno Yuson
characters.description: A werewolf who dates Enid in season 2. Absence Makes the Heart Go Yonder: With his girlfriend Sofia back in the Philippines, Bruno's eye wanders to Enid whom he begins dating. She'snothappy when she learns he's been lying to her and even less happy when Sofia shows up. Asian Rudeness: A Filipino young man who acts like a nice guy on the outside, but is actually a lying, unfaithful cheater who gets too coddled with Enid despite already having a girlfriend back in the Philippines. Bilingual Backfire: He attempts to use Tagalog when contacting Sofia by phone and passing it off as his mother calling him. Wednesday, in Enid's body, reveals that she can understand him. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: On the surface, Bruno seems like a cool and nice guy who genuinely likes Enid, but it is revealed that he is secretly a jerk who already has a girlfriend, Sofia, and tries to lie to Enid about it when caught.

characters.name: Larissa Weems
characters.description: The headmistress of Nevermore Academy and former roommate of Morticia Addams.In Season 2, it's revealed that she is a distant relative of the Addamses', being Wednesday's 13th cousin twice removed. Adaptational Job Change: In the original Addams Family comics strips, Miss Weems was Wednesday and Pugsley's nanny. In the show, she is the headmistress of Nevermore Academy. Although, she does tend to act as a babysitter towards Wednesday at times, looking closely after her in attempts to keep her out of trouble. Alas, Poor Villain:For a given measure of "Villain", anyway. Despite her past misdeeds and animosity towards Wednesday, Weems' death is shown in a poignant light and everyone is shocked at the revelation that she's been murdered. Bait-and-Switch Tyrant: The first few episodes sure paint Weems in a sinister light bycovering up Rowan's murder, on behalf of the school and his family, and she remains anObstructive Bureaucratthroughout the first season, but all things considered, she is much more lenient with Wednesday's reckless behavior than she could be if she was genuinely antagonistic. Wednesday gets a pass for many things, including endangering her classmates, with no more than a warning, andeven when she blows up her last chance by kidnapping and torturing a suspect, Weems still has enough trust in her abilities to participate in her plan to weed out the true mastermind. All in all, more aReasonable Authority Figurethan aDean Bitterman. The Bus Came Back: Having been absent from the first half of the season due to her death, Weems makes an unexpected return as Wednesday’s spirit guide.

characters.name: Barry Dort
characters.description: The new principal of Nevermore, followingLarissa Weems' death. Affably Evil: Dort is a very friendly and positive person, who legitimately wants to bring the school together and return it to the old way it was before Weems. Problem is, he is more than willing to manipulate, intimidate, and threaten people into helping him achieve his goals.That being said... All for Nothing: All of Dort's scheming since the start of Season 2 ultimately amount to nothing.He finally gets exposed as the true mastermind of Morning Song when Bianca uses her siren song to force him to confess his crimes.Due to being under Bianca's spells, Dort is forced to confess he was nothing more than a con man who wanted to steal Hester Frump's fortune and even killed one of his minions to avoid splitting the loot with him. Any good will that Nevermore Academy had for him is instantly gone for good.He takes Bianca as a hostage and tries to flee, but thanks to Ajax, Dort is turned to stone and then crushed by a chandelier, killing him. He finally gets exposed as the true mastermind of Morning Song when Bianca uses her siren song to force him to confess his crimes. Due to being under Bianca's spells, Dort is forced to confess he was nothing more than a con man who wanted to steal Hester Frump's fortune and even killed one of his minions to avoid splitting the loot with him. Any good will that Nevermore Academy had for him is instantly gone for good.

characters.name: Isadora Capri
characters.description: A werewolf who is Nevermore's music teacher. Child Prodigy: Wrote her first classical album at the age of 10. Dark and Troubled Past: She was once in a relationship with a Hyde, who tried to kill her at the command of his jealous master. Her father was also a Hyde. Elegant Classical Musician: A skilled pianist who's played by the beautiful Billie Piper. Former Child Star: She was an accomplished musician even as a child but stopped when the constant drive for success started suffocating her.

characters.name: Orloff
characters.description: The oldest teacher at Nevermore. And Show It to You: Orloff watches the power source of his life support rig get removed through the tank he's in, creating a mechanical version of watching his own heart being torn out. Cool Teacher: Orloff is a warm and caring man who truly wants to help his students. He instantly accepts Agnes and helps her through her issues. Cruel and Unusual Death: He'staken by Isaac who removes his life support and then consumes his brain. Hidden Depths: Initially portrayed as a grumpyStern Teacherwith little patience for misbehaving students at his class, it's revealed that he leads a supporting group for living body parts like him, which includes Thing, to help them handle their existence as disembodied beings, and when a distraught Agnes comes in looking for help, he gives her some much needed advice on accepting and assisting herself despite the fact that she's not a body part like them.

characters.name: Rosaline Rotwood
characters.description: A psychic and a former teacher at Nevermore Academy who is long dead by the events of the series. She is the namesake and original resident of Rotwood Cottage, which Marilyn Thornhill once resided in and which Morticia Addams takes residence in during Season 2. Rotwood's spirit lingers and offers a ritual to those who visit her grave, offering to restore psychic sight to disempowered seers, but leaving a punishment for those who fail the ritual—which initiates a body-swap between Wednesday and Enid when Enid prevents Wednesday from executing the ritual properly.

characters.name: Morticia Addams
characters.description: Matriarch of the Addams family. Accidental Hero:Ends up inadvertently saving the school by stabbing Garrett Gates, since the jealous teen had been instructed by his father to spike the Rave'N's punchbowl withnightshade. Adaptational Superpower Change: As a Seer, she has occasional prophetic dreams of both the past and the future, which is an original element created for this series. She passed this ability on to her daughter. All Girls Want Bad Boys: As a teenager, she got weak in the knees seeing Gomez led away in handcuffs.Because she was in disbelief that he would take the fall for Garrett's death to keep her from having to face an injustice. Beautiful Singing Voice: Morticia cansing, which is no shock as she's played by a Tony Award winning actress. After her duet with Capri, she's complimented on her talent in-universe and notes she usually "only sings at funerals."

characters.name: Gomez Addams
characters.description: Patriarch of the Addams family. Adaptation Personality Change: While still aDashing Hispanic, this version of Gomez is far less of ahamthan previous versions. His most dramatic moments are when he's schmoozing Morticia, and even thenhe does it in a calm, almost whispered cadence that emphasizes tendernessover the grand displays of passion other Gomezes are prone to showing. Affectionate Nickname: AsThe Nicknamerfor his family, he comes up with all kinds of pet names for his daughter. My little stormcloud/death trap for instance. Brought Down to Normal:He had the sameShock and Awepowers as Fester and Pugsley back in his youth, but lost them when Isaac used him as aLiving Batteryfor his machine. Dashing Hispanic: Though no longer conventionally handsome as his younger self in the show, he's still every bit the charmer he's known to be.

characters.name: Lurch
characters.description: The Addamses' loyal butler. Adaptational Attractiveness: He lacks the iconicFrankenstein's Monsterfeatures, looking a lot more like a regular human. Made of Iron: A flashback in Season 2 shows Lurch surviving a car exploding right next to him after Pugsley blows it up with a grenade launcher. The Stoic: Much like Wednesday, nothing seems to make him flinch. Tall, Dark, and Handsome: Very tall, very dark and, unlike his original counterpart, surprisingly good-looking.

characters.name: Thing
characters.description: A disembodied hand considered family by the Addamses'. Adaptational Ugliness: Notwithstanding the fact that he's still a sentient disembodied hand, most versions of Thing are otherwise unblemished hands. This version of Thing has several Frankenstein-esque stitches. Ambiguous Criminal History: Apparently participated in the "Kalamazoo Job" with Uncle Fester in the past, but nothing else is elaborated on about other crimes he has committed. Ascended Extra: Thing is given far more screentime than he ever did in the previous shows and movies, serving as the closest thing to Wednesday's sidekick and somewhat of a mascot to the show. His role gets even bigger in Season 2 when he's revealedto be the reanimated right hand of theBig BadIsaac Night. Back from the Dead: Maybe, considering he's a sentient hand with Frankenstein-like stitching.Played Straightlater, when he's stabbed and brought back to life by Fester electrocuting him.

characters.name: Uncle Fester
characters.description: Wednesday's eccentric paternal uncle. Adaptational Badass: Other versions of Fester have him giving off enough discharge to light a lightbulb in his mouth as just another Addams-esque quirk, withAddams Family Valuesadding that he has an immunity to electrocution. Here this translates intoShock and Awepowers, allowing him to fire lighting from his hands andcan act as aMagical Defibrillatorwhen Thing gets impaled. It's also revealed that he was the one who taught Wednesday swordsmanship. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: He and Thing may have some animosity stemming from the botched Kalamazoo Job,but he desperately tries to save him via hisShock and Awepowers when he's killed and is genuinely happy to see him revived again. Beware the Silly Ones: Uncle Fester may be rather eccentric and strange even among the Addams Family as a result of his numerous lobotomies. He's still an effective career criminal who's on the run for a bank robbery and too comfortable with putting Tyler in a "Romanian sleeper hold". But Now I Must Go: Uncle Fester has to leave Nevermore as quickly as he appeared after Sheriff Galpin and the rest of the police start closing in on him.

characters.name: Grandmama
characters.description: Wednesday's maternal grandmother. Abusive Parent: Morticia's recollections of her childhood don't paint a good image of Hester, who was indicated to be verbally and emotionally abusive of her daughter. Even in adulthood, she remains very critical of Morticia.That treatment is saintly compared to hers of her other daughter Ophelia, though. Adaptational Attractiveness: Grandmama usually is portrayed as adisheveled cronewith unkempt hair and sunken skin. Here, she's portrayed by Joanna Lumley as a sleek, elegant older woman. Granted, this is Morticia's mother, not Gomez's, who is more usually depicted in Addams family media. Adaptational Jerkass: Grandma Addams or Grandma Frump, are usually portrayed as consistently loving to their families, in their own Addams-y way, and, at worst, Grandma Frump was a bit annoying to her son-in-law sometimes. This version of Grandmama is emotionally abusive to her daughter (in a way even the Addamses disapprove of), bigoted towards Normies and Outcasts without powers, and shows no interest in helping her family unless she has something to gain from it. Anti-Role Model: Wednesday idolizes Hester's success and the ruthlessness with which she earned it, but her Grandmama also embodies the kind of bitter and resented woman Wednesday will become if she doesn't let people in.

characters.name: Varicose
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: Grandmama never had her own personal butler in the original comic strips nor has she ever been depicted with one in other adaptations up to this point. Same goes for Hester Frump. Distaff Counterpart: Varicose is clearly akin to Lurch, being a silent and imposing character who performs every domestic duty for Grandmama with no complaints. Lady Looks Like a Dude: Given her boyish short haircut and physical facial features, this may apply to her. The Voiceless: She's quiet her whole time onscreen.

characters.name: Goody Addams
characters.description: An ancestor of the Addams family, whom Wednesday sees in visions. Absurdly Youthful Mother: She looks very young, presumably because she was very young when she died, but to be Wednesday's great-great-etc-grandmother, she must have had a child before she died. However, this might be just her manifesting herself at a younger age. All Relatives Share a Surname: While it's implied that psychic powers come fromWednesday's matrilineal line, she is an Addams. Ambiguous Situation: It's not entirely clear if she's manifesting herself at the age she died, or if she's deliberately deaging herself to address her descendant Wednesday. Arch-Enemy: She's this for Joseph Crackstone, who calls her "Lucifer's Mistress herself" and is eventually killed and cursed by her.

characters.name: Surprise Distant Relative
characters.description: The headmistress of Nevermore Academy and former roommate of Morticia Addams. In Season 2, it's revealed that she is a distant relative of the Addamses', being Wednesday's 13th cousin twice removed.

characters.name: Dr. Valerie Kinbott
characters.description: Wednesday's therapist and the go-to counselor for Nevermore's students. Armor-Piercing Question: She asks why Wednesday, who makes claims of being cold-hearted and wanting to be distant from people, would keep on making visits to Eugene while he is in a coma. Wednesday doesn't have an answer for that. He Knows Too Much: She iskilled by the Hyde after Wednesday accuses her of controlling a Hyde. While Wednesday's accusation was off, it lets Kinbott know that the monster was a Hyde. Hidden Depths: She apparently has a fondness for taxidermy art that she keeps well hidden. No explanation for this interest is forthcoming. Nice Girl: She cares very much about her patients and wants to see them improve and is nice enough that she even gets through to Wednesday.

characters.name: Mayor Noble Walker
characters.description: The former sheriff and current mayor of Jericho. Alas, Poor Villain:For a given measure of "villain" anyway. Despite his role in covering up the true circumstances of Garrett Gates' murder, his death at Laurel's hands is played sympathetically and his own funeral is asorrowful affair(not helped by it raining) that makes one feel sorry for his son Lucas. Character Tics: He visibly pouts his lips whenever he is put in a tight spot. The Cloudcuckoolander Was Right: According to Donovan Galpin, Noble would often come up with wild theories for cases he investigated when he was the sheriff, most of which never panned out.However, Noble is the first person to realize that Laurel Gates isn't dead, which results in her killing him. Dirty Cop:Walker knew of the Gates' plan to poison the Nevermore students with nightshade, and that Garrett had actually died from nightshade poison. Walker covered it up because he was in Ansel Gates' pocket.

characters.name: Lucas Walker
characters.description: Mayor Walker's son, who works at Pilgrim World. Curb-Stomp Battle: Not once, but twice does he and his lackeys end of on the receiving end of one by Wednesday. Enemy Mine: Still hates Wednesday by the end of Season 1,but is willing to give Wednesday the clues to the murder mystery that his dad ended up being killed for as he (obviously) wants to find his father's killer and hates them even more. Foil: To Tyler, who is introduced in the same scene as Lucas. Lucas is the athletic, hot-headed, African-American leader of aGang of Bullieswho work at Pilgrim World, dislike Nevermore, and get into a fight with Wednesday during their first meeting the Nevermore kids. Tyler is caucasian, less athletic, more of a loner, and is friendly to Wednesday while seeming non-judgmental about her attendance at Nevermore. Furthermore, later episodes also give themHidden Depthsin opposite directions by having Lucasgrow nicerwhile also revealing that Tyler once bullied the Nevermore kids. Finally,Lucas really is human and Tyler is a remorseless monster. Oppose What You Suffered: Though the show does not show African-American Lucas being subjected to any racist abuse himself,he isn't just the first of the bullies to become uneasy about ruining the outcasts' party, but is mortified when his co-bullies hurl discriminatory abuse at Enid, and does not associate with them afterwards.

characters.name: Ritchie Santiago
characters.description: The current sheriff of Jericho following Galpin's fall from grace. Black Boss Lady: A Black woman and the new sheriff. Only Sane Woman: She's one of the only adult figures to have her priorities in the right place. Police Are Useless: Downplayed. She's more reasonable than Galpin and does try to help the population, but things are often one step ahead of her.

characters.name: Sister Arlene
characters.description: A employee of Pilgrim World. Uncertain Doom: She is last seen confronting Isaac in Pilgrim World, with it being left unknown if he devoured her brain.

characters.name: Sheriff Donovan Galpin
characters.description: Sheriff to the town of Jericho, who has a particular dislike for the Addamses. Ambiguous Situation:Just how aware he was of his son being the Hyde (and thus responsible for the murders he's trying to solve) is ultimately left ambiguous. Bigot with a Crush:Despite his utter hatred of outcasts, he fell in love with the most dangerous type of outcast, a Hyde. Season 2 reveals that Francoise did not initially tell him that she was a Hyde, as she yearned for a normal life with him. Dropped a Bridge on Him:He's found dead at the beginning of Season 2. Eye Scream:Both of his eyes are gouged by ravens.

characters.name: Joseph Crackstone
characters.description: The founder of Jericho who is intent on killing all outcasts. Arch-Enemy: For Goody Addams, whom he calls "Lucifer's Mistress herself". He is eventually killed and cursed by her to prevent his return. This is later extended to Goody's descendant, Wednesday, who is destined to fight him as the season'sFinal Bossand deliver the final killing blow to cast him out for good. Boomerang Bigot: He screams at the students of Nevermore that they are abominations and demons even after becoming an undead monstrosity powered only by black magic, all without a single shred of self-awareness. Big "SHUT UP!":When Laurel talks a bit too much for comfort, he roars"SILENCE, WOMAAAAAAAN!!!!!!"at the top of his lungs. Broken Pedestal: Downplayed, and for laughs too! Right after Crackstone silences Laurel Gates and threatens to kill her, Laurel immediately backs off, quipping "Never meet your heroes." Though it's a bit ambiguous if she really felt betrayed or still looked up to the evil pilgrim.

characters.name: Garrett Gates
characters.description: The son of the wealthiest family in Jericho who died under suspicious circumstances in 1990. Abhorrent Admirer: Morticia describes him in such terms — he didn't take her rejection for an answer and was willing to murder the guy whose feelings she reciprocated. Accidental Murder: Morticia grabbed a sword to defend Gomez from Garrett, accidentally impaling him. It's not what killed him, but everyone thought it was. Crazy Jealous Guy: He went directly after Gomez to kill him, abandoning his initial plan to spike the punch which would kill the whole school, because he hated how close he was to Morticia. Dating What Daddy Hates: Though he never dated Morticia he wanted to, which caused tension between him and his outcast-hating father.

characters.name: Laurel Gates
characters.description: The sister of Garrett Gates and the descendant of Joseph Crackstone who poses as a botany teacher in Nevermore under the alias "Marilyn Thornill." She is the mastermind behind the Hyde killings taking place in Season 1.

characters.name: Dr. Rachel Fairburn
characters.description: The chief psychiatrist at Willow Hill. Affably Evil: She seems civil to Wednesday and eager to help redeem Tyler and her other patients and is protective of Dr. Stonehearst even at her most sinister, but she gloatingly locks Fester in a cell with a zombie for spying on her and is experimenting on the people she claims to be helping. The Dragon:She works for Judi Stonehearst, the true mastermind of the LOIS project. Eaten Alive:By Slurp when he catches her off guard. He quickly devours Augustus's brain next. Hoist by Her Own Petard:Her very stupid decision to put a brain-eating zombie in a cell just to torment Fester results in the entirely foreseeable consequence of said zombie escaping and coming for her.

characters.name: Augustus Stonehearst
characters.description: The former chief physician of Willow Hill and the founder of the LOIS Project. Asshole Victim: Played with.He was definitely responsible for a great many events throughout Season 2, but by the time Isaac devours his brain, he's long since been reduced to a helpless wheelchair-bound old man who can hardly cling on to any remaining shred of sanity. Eaten Alive:After Isaac eats Fairburn's brain, he goes after Augustus next. Understandably, the poor old chap is completely unable to defend himself. Face Death with Despair:Augustus recognizes Isaac and is terrified as the zombie comes for him. He's too helpless to resist and dies in agonized terror. Greater-Scope Villain: Of Season 2. He launched the secret LOIS (Long-Term Outcast Integration Study) project, with the goal was to transfer the supernatural abilities of Outcasts to normies like himselfand later, his daughter Judi. He is also the one responsible for faking Francoise's death and keeping her at Willow Hill, presumably leading to the Galpin family falling apart and Tyler's path to villainy, and Isaac Night's mentor who helped him build his illegal lab. This makes him responsible in some way for four out of five main villains of the season.

characters.name: Chet Latoy / Kansas City Scalper
characters.description: An infamous serial killer, whom Wednesday targets at the beginning of Season 2. Collector of the Strange: He has a basement withcreepy dollsall set up for a tea party. It's implied that their hair is made fromall his victims' hair. Mugging the Monster: He kidnaps Wednesday intending to make her his next victim, unaware that she let herself beCaptured on Purpose. It doesn't take long before she (and Thing) defeat him. Starter Villain: For Season 2. He's the first villain Wednesday faces, but is quickly defeated before the season premiere ends. Would Hurt a Child: He's been preying on girls for a good long while.

characters.name: Ron Kruger
characters.description: A cadet master of a rival Boy Scouts team that competes with Nevermore students for the right to camp at Camp Jericho during their school field trip. Asshole Victim: Downplayed. Ron is a rude, verbally abusive, and sexistDrill Sergeant Nastywhogets his brain eaten by Slurp/Issac after accidentally stumbling upon him in Pugsley's tent during an attempt to sabotage Nevermore students' camping trip but regardless he is mourned by his cadets. Casting Gag: In the Brazilian dub, he's voiced by Élcio Romar, who voiced no other than Sergeant Hartman inFull Metal Jacket. Drill Sergeant Nasty: Ron may be a cadet master instead of a drill sergeant, but he exhibits all the behaviours of one as he treats his cadets like soldiers under his command and is verbally abusive towards them when they fail (such as calling them worthless when they lose to Wednesday). They still seem upset by his fate. Even Evil Can Be Loved: "Evil" is a stretch, but he's aJerkass, sexist and verbally abusiveDrill Sergeant Nastywho nevertheless is well-respected by his cadets.After he's killed by Slurp/Issac, his cadets are shown saluting him as his corpse is taken.

characters.name: Kruger's cadets
characters.description: A group of Boy Scouts led by Ron Kruger that had a contract to use the same camp that the outcasts did and, in order to solve the double booking, competes with Nevermore students for the right to camp at Camp Jericho during their school field trip. Anti-Villain: They don't seem to be particularly bad kids, they just happen to be under the tutelage of an asshole. Badass Normal: They're all normies with no powers, but are still able to use their Boy Scout skills to compete with the Outcast team evenly, almost beating them at the game for the camp. I Was Beaten by a Girl: Invoked by Kruger, who admonishes them for losing the competition for the camp, and to a girl no less, as Wednesday's improvised zipline and knocking the member near the finish spot unconscious was what cost them the victory. Sympathy for the Hero: When a group of them overhears Ajax discussing with Enid how she grew distant from him but wasn't able to break up with him and just kept avoiding him instead, one of them comments that he "(feels) bad for that gorgon".

characters.name: Dalton
characters.description: A student at Nancy Reagan High School who tormented Pugsley while he and Wednesday attended the school. 1-Dimensional Thinking: He likely would have escaped the piranha swarm if he'd swum to thesideof the pool like his fellows, rather than swimming all the way to the ladder at the other end. Posssibly justified in thatpeople often make life-threatening mistakes when they panic, and he had every reason to panic. Asshole Victim: The narrative shows little sympathy for his genital mutilation, and when Wednesday's psychologist questions her about the incident and how it left to a boy losing a testicle, the girl shows no remorse and declares she "did the world a favor, people like Dalton shouldn't be allowed to procreate". Crippling Castration: Loses a testicle to Wednesday's piranha swarm, which in her words was a favor to the world, as "people like Dalton should not be allowed to procreate". Though if he still has one testicle, he can still be able to have children once he recovers. Groin Attack: His fate is getting piranhas sicced on him by Wednesday. Guess what the piranhas aim for?

characters.name: The Crow
characters.description: A mysterious crow with heavy scarring on the right side of its face, including a giant white eyeball. It serves the Avian behindthe murders of Carl and Donovanand leads the other birds on missions. Ambiguous Situation:It shows up again at the very end of the second season, though it's hard to say whether or not it's still evil or whether it's following the trio searching for Enid. Attack Animal: It primarily carries out espionage and murder for the Avian master. Creepy Crows: It's even creepy than the other crows under the Avian's command due to its scarred face. The Dragon: It leads the other crows on behalf of their Avian master.

characters.name: Esther Sinclair
characters.description: Enid's overbearing mother. Abusive Parents: She's incredibly insulting and passive aggressive towards Enid, barely making an effort to hide her disappointment in her inability to transform. Poor Enid looks constantly close to tears every time she's around her. Foil: To Morticia. While both are mothers that aren't on the best terms with their children, Esther is much more abrasive and makes it very clear thatshe's disappointed in Enidwhile Morticia shows nothing but support to Wednesday and is clearly proud of her accomplishments. Morticia wants Wednesday to forge her own path, while Esther wants Enid to follow her in "wolfing out". At the end of parents' weekend, Morticiafinallyparts on good terms with Wednesday and reaffirms the fact that she will always be there for her while Esther silently leaves inTranquil Furyafter Enidfinally stands up to her. Hate Sink: Her only scene shows her to be a passive-aggressive, abusive mother who goes out of her way to berate her own daughter. Made all the worse when it'sEnidwe're talking about. Have You Tried Not Being a Monster?: Or rather "Have you tried being a monster?" She tries to send her daughter to what is explicitly referred to as a conversion camp to cure her of her inability to wolf out.However, Enid does eventually wolf out, which contradicts the message of the pre-established allegory.

characters.name: Murray Sinclair
characters.description: Good Parents: He proves to love his daughter unconditionally and want her to be herself, in contrast to his wife. For example, he congratulates Enid for standing up to her mother. Loving Parent, Cruel Parent: Definitely the Loving (supportive, encouraging) to Esther's Cruel. The Quiet One: He lets his wife do all the talking up until the end of their visit. Given howopinionatedEsther can be, this silence may be more of a survival tactic than a choice.

characters.name: Arnold Hunt / Gideon Sterling
characters.description: The mysterious leader of the Morning Song cult, or so we are lead to believe at first. While he isThe Ghostfor most of the series, his presence ties into Bianca's personal subplot as she needs to help her mother hide from him. Alas, Poor Villain:His final moments have him realizing that he too was scammed by Barry Dort as part of the latter's Morning Song cult and he rightfully demands Dort split the money. Except Dort has other plans and has him burned to death. Arc Villain:Ultimately subverted. Both seasons build him up as the one behind the events of the Morning Song storyline untilWoe Me The Moneyreveals that he was hired by Barry Dort to be the cult's public face. Con Man: A flashback showshim outright telling Dort his business pitch sounds like a cult but still having little hesitation or remorse before agreeing to join him. The Dragon:What heactuallyis, though even Bianca and Gabrielle didn't know he was Dort's reluctantPuppet Kinguntil Dort himself revealed it.

characters.name: Gabrielle Barclay
characters.description: Bianca's mother and a member of the Morning Song cult. She later defects in Season 2. Brought Down to Normal: It is mentioned that she overused her Siren Song due to her work in the Morning Song Cult. This explains why she had to rely on Bianca to use her powers on other people for her protection instead of doing it herself. Characterization Marches On: The difference in how she comes off in both Seasons are very staggering. When she first appears in Season 1, she is quite cold and strict to her daughter whom she disapproves of her choices, indicating she is anAbusive Parentto her daughter with Bianca saying she is done with both Morning Song and her. But in Season 2, she seems so scared and vulnerable, heavily reliant on her daughter to protect her. Cult Defector: She had a crisis of conscience offscreen and decided to leave the Morning Song, hiding with her daughter's help. The Dragon: She was in a relationship with Gideon (who ironically turned out to beThe Dragonfor Dort) and was therefore his greatest asset in finding and indoctrinating more cult members. However, Bianca convinces her to leave Morning Song around the beginning of Season 2.
